newsitem.title: UK: Timing and majorities of past British elections.
newsitem.headline: Timing and majorities of past British elections.

text.p: Following are data on the timing of, and majorities after, recent British elections -

Intervals in days at recent elections 1974 (October) - 2 days between announcement of election (September 18) to the dissolution (September 20) 32 days between dissolution and parliament assembling (September 20 to October 22) 12 days between polling day and parliament assembling (October 10 to October 22) 1979 - 9 days (March 29 to April 7), 32 days (April 7 and May 9), 6 days (May 3 to May 9) 1983 - 4 days (May 9 to May 13), 33 days (May 13 to June 15), 6 days (June 9 to June 15) 1987 - 7 days (May 11 to May 18), 30 days (May 18 to June 17), 6 days (June 11 to June 17) 1992 - 5 days (March 11 to March 16), 42 days (March 16 to April 27), 18 days (April 9 to April 27)
1974 (October) - Conservative 277 (35.8 percent), Labour 319 (39.2 percent), Liberal 13, others 26. Labour majority of three. Turnout 72.8 percent
1979 - Conservatives 339 (43.9 percent), Labour 269 (36.9 percent), Liberal 11, others 16. Majority 43. Turnout 76.0 percent
1983 - Conservatives 397 (42.4 percent), Labour 209 (27.6 percent), Social Democrat Party/Liberal alliance 23, others 21. Majority 144 (largest Conservative majority since 1935). Turnout 72.7 percent
1987 - Conservatives 375 (42.3 pct), Labour 229 (30.8 pct), Liberal/Social Democrat Alliance 22, others 23. Majority 101. Turnout 75.3 percent. (Conservative speaker not included)
1992 - Conservatives 336 (41.9 pct of vote), Labour 271 (34.4 pct), Liberal Democrat 20, others 24. Majority 21. Turnout 77.7 percent
